purpose: Qualify shuffled English inferential cards as source-supported, semantically recoverable task materials while measuring lexical-ASR shortcut risk on a deterministic held-out translation split.

rejected_designs.design: first semantic cards with Whisper-tiny lexical matching
first semantic cards with shipped Whisper-base full-turn matching

rejected_designs.reason_rejected: The certifying translations were also used during card authoring, so the score was in-sample.
The untouched translation holdout exposed residual lexical restatement.

writer_forbidden_inputs: all prior card artifacts and audits
ground truth, oracle, and verifier outputs

final_card_construct.name: inferential consequence
final_card_construct.description: Each card states a source-entailed counterfactual, implication, falsifiable policy-logic test, or premise/outcome tension rather than summarizing or translating the speech.

lexical_shortcut_preflight.pipeline: Energy VAD, YuNet/SFace 742-way identity, VoxLingua language, shipped Whisper-base full-turn English translation, and maximum-weight one-to-one card assignment over TF-IDF cosine, character-trigram Jaccard, and word Jaccard.

semantic_ceiling_control.input: 86 complete official transcripts in original languages plus 86 shuffled final inferential cards; identifiers independently shuffled; no speaker identity or turn order.
semantic_ceiling_control.network: sealed calibration network; no external content was obtained

provenance_note: The cards are explicitly model-authored and cross-model-qualified auxiliary input materials, not official quotations or independent ground-truth labels. The hidden card-to-turn mapping remains the fixed deterministic shuffle of the 86 official interventions.
